LanguageData.VM_Settings_TrackByIngredientOverlapTool: Per-meal variety is scored by how many ingredients overlap with the pawn's recent meals. Two separate windows: ingredient scoring always compares against the last 6 meals (fixed, all tiers); the full meal-history queue (expectation-tier × memory multiplier) is kept for the meal-type-novelty bonus and the details UI. Trivial swaps give partial credit; fully-different meals count as fresh; repeats count as stale.
LanguageData.VM_Settings_NonControlledPawnsLabel: Non controlled pawns also have variety need:
LanguageData.VM_Settings_FoodDrugsOnceLabel: Foods that are also drugs are stored in memory just once:
LanguageData.VM_Settings_FoodDrugsOnceTooltip: Foods that also serve as drugs are stored in memory only once. This allows for a scheduled intake of these substances without diminishing variety, while still enjoying the benefits of having them considered as variety if the pawns likes them as food.
LanguageData.VM_Settings_PreferVarietyTooltip: Cooks rotate ingredients across meals and mix distinct ThingDefs within a single meal. Mixing only applies to bills with 'Allow mixing ingredients' enabled — bills without mixing still get variety-weighted sort order but remain single-ingredient per slot.
LanguageData.VM_Settings_StackByIngredientsTooltip: When enabled, cooked meals with different ingredient sets do NOT stack together in storage — each distinct ingredient combo keeps its own stack. Required for the per-meal variety score to work correctly (otherwise all meals of a type merge into one bag and ingredient history is lost). Disable only if you want vanilla stacking behavior.
LanguageData.VM_Settings_ClusterSimilarMealsLabel: Count different quality meals as the same meal type:
LanguageData.VM_Settings_ClusterSimilarMealsExample: ^For example, Fine and Lavish meals will counted as one type
LanguageData.VM_Settings_NumIngredientsTooltip: Maximum distinct ingredient ThingDefs the cook will stuff into a single produced meal when 'Cooks use different ingredients' is on. Higher values = more variety per plate but harder pantry management. Vanilla caps at 3; setting this lower throttles the mod's mixing behavior.
LanguageData.VM_Settings_CookingMemoryDepthTooltip: How many recent meals each cook remembers when picking ingredients for the next one. Higher = wider rotation (cook avoids repeating ingredients across more past meals). Purely a cooking-AI knob — does NOT affect the pawn-side variety mood window.
LanguageData.VM_Settings_ExpectationExplanation: Each value drives two things for that tier: (1) how many past meals the pawn remembers (queue size = value × memory multiplier), and (2) how picky their palate is (palate threshold = clamp((value − 3)/25, 0, 0.50)). Higher values make the tier harder to satisfy on both axes. Defaults: Noble → palate 0.48, remembers ~34 meals.
LanguageData.VM_Settings_LowExpectationFloorTooltip: Hard floor on expected variety count after all tier / slave / prisoner / gourmand modifiers. Keeps tribal / Naked Brutality starts from dropping to 1–2 and trivializing early-game food variety. Raise to make the early game harder; lower to give low-expectation colonies an easier ride.
LanguageData.VM_Settings_SlaveExpectedVarietyLabel: Slave expected variety (% of tier, default 65%):
LanguageData.VM_Settings_SlaveExpectedVarietyTooltip: Percentage applied to the slave's tier value. Scales both expected-variety count AND palate threshold. 100% = same as a free pawn of the same tier; 50% = half as picky.
LanguageData.VM_Settings_PrisonerExpectedVarietyLabel: Prisoner expected variety (% of tier, default 50%):
LanguageData.VM_Settings_PrisonerExpectedVarietyToolt: Percentage applied to the prisoner's tier value. Scales both expected-variety count AND palate threshold. 100% = same as a free pawn of the same tier; 50% = half as picky.
LanguageData.VM_Settings_HalveVarietyMoodTooltip: Cuts the food-variety mood thought weight in half (multiplier 2.0 → 1.0). The same variety score produces half the mood swing, both positive and negative. Use for a softer difficulty pass.
LanguageData.VM_Settings_MoreVarietyMemoryTooltip: Bumps the memory multiplier from 2.25 to 2.75. Pawns remember more past meals (bigger queue), but the mood-at-100% ceiling scales up too, so the same variety score reaches a higher mood. Net effect: easier to maintain high variety mood at steady state.
